tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H19): Hand-written 2SM tcgen05 TF32 pair kernel: one pass over the whole batch (N = Bpad <= 512) for 131 < B <= 512, evict_first W stream. Start from tc_small.cu in r2-e1-tc05-ef-small and keep its B <= 131 path, CUTLASS 256x192 for B > 512, binding and dispatch unchanged. Add tc_pair.cu: launch 144 CTAs as 72 clusters of 2 (cudaLaunchKernelEx, cluster dims 2x1x1), 1 CTA per SM, 128 threads. CTA rank r owns W rows m0 = 256*cluster + 128*r (so the pair is the UMMA M = 256) and, for each UMMA i of N_i (N_0 = min(Bpad, 256), N_1 = Bpad - 256 if Bpad > 256; Bpad = B rounded up to 16; N_i multiple of 16, >= 32), emb rows [sum_{j<i} N_j + r*N_i/2, +N_i/2). Per stage per CTA: kbs x (16 KB W + Bpad/2 x 128 B emb), both via TMA with SWIZZLE_128B and CU_TENSOR_MAP_DATA_TYPE_TFLOAT32 (FLOAT32 truncates and fails: see r2 findings); W with createpolicy evict_first cache hint, emb unhinted. Choose kbs as the largest of 4/3/2/1 that leaves >= 3 stages in 224 KB (B=192: kbs 2 with 3-4 stages or kbs 1 with 7). Use cta_group::2 PTX: tcgen05.alloc.cta_group::2 of 512 columns (power of 2 >= Bpad) issued in both CTAs as CUTLASS does; the leader (rank 0) issues tcgen05.mma.cta_group::2.kind::tf32 with M=256, N=N_i, four per 32-wide k-block per UMMA, TMEM column offset sum_{j<i} N_j; the full barrier of each stage lives in the leader, both CTAs' TMA loads complete_tx on it through its shared::cluster address (mapa), expect_tx = both CTAs' stage bytes; the leader's tcgen05.commit.cta_group::2 ... .multicast::cluster with ctaMask 0b11 arrives at the empty barrier of both CTAs, each producer waits on its own. Read the exact PTX forms (fences, cluster barrier at start and before exit, instruction descriptor bits for M=256 / cta_group::2, UMMA smem descriptors for the SW128 K-major atoms) from CUTLASS 4.4.1 headers: cute/arch/mma_sm100_umma.hpp, cute/arch/mma_sm100_desc.hpp, cutlass/gemm/collective/sm100_mma_warpspecialized.hpp, cutlass/pipeline/sm100_pipeline.hpp. There is no public tcgen05 example in read_example. Epilogue as tc_small: each warp reads its 32 TMEM lanes (W rows) in 16-column chunks, adds bias, stores out_c[b*3072 + m - c*3072] for b < B; c = m0/3072 is uniform per CTA (3072 % 128 == 0). Steps: (1) correctness at B = 132, 192, 211, 256, 373, 384, 449, 512 vs torch fp64, report max |err| per B (must be <= 1.7e-3). (2) In-kernel clock64 and %globaltimer deltas (first TMA issue to last store, thread 0 of each CTA, max over CTAs written to a diagnostic buffer in probes only) to report cycles, the rented SM clock and per-clock efficiency = 2*128*Bpad*3072 / (cycles * 4096) per CTA. (3) Interleaved probe, 3 rounds, harness flush + CUPTI: the new kernel vs the r2 dispatch (tc_small at 192/211, CUTLASS 256x192/256x256 at 373-512) at B = 192, 211, 256, 373, 384, 449, 512; also kbs/stage variants at 192 and 512. (4) Predict the portal time per B as max(1.05 x rented time if DRAM-bound, cycles / 1.55 GHz) and state it in the card. (5) Dispatch 131 < B <= 512 to tc_pair only where it wins by >= 5% in cycles; run_tests 16/16; build must stay under 300 s (the LOCAL target needs the __CUDA_ARCH_FEAT_SM100_ALL guard). Stretch (H22, only if steps 1-5 are done): a persistent variant doing two batch halves per pair for 691-919, measured the same way; do not let it delay the submission candidate. Success: 16/16 correct with max |err| <= 1.7e-3; in the interleaved probe, B = 192/211 <= 46 us rented (DRAM-bound), B = 373/384 <= 52 us rented with >= 70% per-clock efficiency, B = 449/512 <= 62/68 us rented; predicted portal M-band geomean <= 52 us (from 66.6). Refuted if: The pair kernel's cycles at 373-512 are within 10% of the CUTLASS 256x192/256x256 tiles (efficiency <= 60% per clock), or B = 192/211 stay above 48 us rented with >= 6 stages, meaning one-pass wide tiles do not beat persistent padded tiles and the limiter is elsewhere (H20/H21). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H21): Microbenchmarks in cycles: 1SM vs 2SM UMMA TF32 rate from resident operands, cost of the TMA feed, and ring-depth slope of tc_small. Probe-only session; no submission candidate. All timings in SM cycles (clock64 around the mainloop in the MMA-issuing thread, plus %globaltimer to report the rented SM clock for every run; run each case 3 times interleaved and report the clock). (a) Resident-operand UMMA rate: strip tc_small's TMA producer; fill one stage of W and emb smem once (any values), then issue the full 96 k-blocks x 4 UMMAs of 1SM 128xN kind::tf32 against that stage with commits every k-block as in the real kernel, for N = 128, 192, 256. Report FLOP/clk/SM vs the 4096 peak. Repeat with cta_group::2 256xN (cluster of 2, leader issues, both CTAs hold operands; mirror CUTLASS's sm100 PTX forms from cute/arch/mma_sm100_umma.hpp) for N = 128, 192, 256; report per-SM efficiency. (b) TMA feed from L2: same loops but with the real coupled TMA ring, W replaced by a 148 x 128 x 3072 fp32 buffer (227 MB -> 232 MB is too large to be L2-resident, so instead give every CTA the same 128 W rows: 1.5 MB, L2-resident) and emb as today; this isolates the smem-port and TMA-issue cost from DRAM. Compare 1SM 128x192 kbs=1 5 stages (the shipped B=192 config) against kbs=2 (if the smem fits with the small W) and against a 2SM 256x192 ring where each CTA holds 96 emb rows. (c) Ring-depth slope on the real tc_small at B = 192 and 256 with real W from DRAM (harness flush): force stages = 3, 4, 5 at kbs=1 and report cycles per k-block; a steep slope means latency-bound, a flat one means issue/operand-bound. (d) emb L2 hot-spotting, diagnostic only: at B = 192 and 256, run tc_small unchanged vs a variant whose tensor map points each CTA at its own copy of emb (a scratch buffer holding emb replicated 144 times, filled outside the timed region); if private copies are >= 10% fewer cycles, the shared-line L2 contention is real and E3's multicast is the fix. Write every number into findings with the clock it ran at and the per-clock efficiency; name the limiter for the B = 192 case (ring depth, UMMA shape, smem port, or emb L2). Success: Each of (a)-(d) reported in cycles with the measured clock, and a one-line verdict on what limits tc_small at B = 192-256: e.g. resident 1SM 128x192 >= 90% and TMA-fed 1SM <= 60% while 2SM-fed >= 75% supports H21; a steep stage slope supports the ring-depth explanation; private emb copies >= 10% faster supports H20. Refuted if: Resident 1SM 128x192 is already <= 70% of 4096 FLOP/clk (then the UMMA shape, not the feed, is the limiter and H21's first clause is false), or 2SM-fed is no better per SM than 1SM-fed (then the 2SM route of H19 gains nothing from operand traffic). This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. Experiment E3 (tests H20): tc_small with TMA multicast of the emb k-block across a 2-CTA cluster for 131 < B <= 256. Minimal change to tc_small.cu, keep everything else (1SM UMMA, kbs rule, evict_first W, epilogue) identical. Launch the 144 CTAs as 72 clusters of 2 (cudaLaunchKernelEx, cluster dims 2x1x1); CTAs 2p and 2p+1 keep their own W tiles (rows 128*(2p) and 128*(2p+1)). For each stage, CTA rank r loads emb rows [r*Bpad/2, (r+1)*Bpad/2) of each k-block with cp.async.bulk.tensor.2d.shared::cluster.global.mbarrier::complete_tx::bytes.multicast::cluster, ctaMask 0b11, into the same smem offset in both CTAs, so each CTA receives the full Bpad rows while L2 traffic for emb halves. Each CTA's full barrier expects its own W bytes plus the full emb bytes of the stage (both halves arrive from the two producers). Empty barrier: a producer may overwrite a stage only when both CTAs' MMAs have consumed it, so init each empty barrier with count 2 and have each CTA's MMA thread commit with tcgen05.commit.cta_group::1 ... .multicast::cluster ctaMask 0b11 (one arrival in each CTA). Add a cluster barrier (barrier.cluster.arrive/wait) after mbarrier init and before exit so no CTA leaves while its peer can still write its smem. Bpad/2 must be a multiple of 8 rows for the SW128 atoms: use Bpad rounded to 32 for this variant (B = 192 -> 192, 211 -> 224, 256 -> 256; emb rows beyond B zero-filled by TMA OOB). Measure with in-kernel clock64 + %globaltimer (report the rented clock) in one interleaved probe, 3 rounds, harness flush + CUPTI: multicast vs unchanged tc_small at B = 132, 192, 211, 256. Also try kbs=2 at 192 if the stage still fits (it will not, smem is unchanged; note it). Report cycles, per-clock efficiency = 2*128*Bpad*3072/(cycles*4096), max |err| vs fp64 per B (<= 1.7e-3), and the predicted portal time = max(1.05 x rented DRAM-bound time, cycles / 1.55 GHz). If multicast wins by >= 5% in cycles at 192 and 211, package it as a candidate: dispatch 131 < B <= 256 to the multicast variant, B <= 131 unchanged, B > 256 unchanged, run_tests 16/16, card paths with cluster: 2 and w: ef. Otherwise record the negative result and no candidate. Success: >= 10% fewer cycles than tc_small at B = 192 and 211 (and 256), 16/16 correct, error <= 1.7e-3: emb L2 re-read is a confirmed M-band limiter and the pair kernel of E1 should also multicast emb across pairs. Refuted if: Multicast changes cycles by <= 3% at 192/211/256 in the interleaved probe: emb L2 traffic is not the limiter (ring depth or UMMA shape are, see E2) and E1 need not add multicast.
